rationale: Objective is wall-clock latency_ms of the frozen batch=1 FP32 forward (TF32 and cudnn benchmark disabled, exact top-1), so only structure-preserving rewrites of the observed execution are eligible; precision or algorithm-policy changes are not. In the observed run every one of the 20 aten.conv2d invocations is immediately followed by an eval-mode BatchNorm2d inside a ResNetConvLayer or ResNetShortCut module: 643.52us conv + 43.84us batch_norm (20 kernels + 20 module dispatches inside the timed region) out of the 731.39us diagnostic total. The chosen joint boundary is that conv-epilogue chain at all 20 sites. The edits are mutually dependent, which is why this is one joint candidate rather than two: rescaling conv weights while keeping the BN affine corrupts logits, and removing the BN without folding it into the conv corrupts logits; only the closed transform (fold per-channel scale/shift into conv weight, give the bias-less convs a folded bias, drop the BN call) preserves semantics and only together do they remove work. This is not a blanket operator-name policy: it is anchored to this workload's measured conv-BN adjacency, the 6.0% batch_norm kernel share and the launch/dispatch cost that a wall-latency metric charges. The boundary also contains the documented stage-3 hot spot (stages.3 is 350.46us inclusive, 47.9% of the run; its convs alone are 334.97us, 45.8%): the 256->512 stride-2 conv at 115.97us runs at ~1.0 TFLOP/s versus 3.2-3.7 TFLOP/s for its identical-FLOP (115.5 MF) downsample siblings at 30.85us and 36.54us, and 512x512x3x3 convs at 7x7 run at 3.4 TFLOP/s versus 12.2 TFLOP/s for the same 231 MF at 28x28, so any shape-preserving FP32 call-path variant for those specific sites belongs inside the same conv groups and must be judged by the same tolerance gate. Conv2d/batch_norm module groups and their aten call groups are included together so the editable boundary covers both sides of the fold at every site; ReLU, residual add_, pooling and classifier calls are outside the fold and untouched.
hypothesis: Folding all 20 eval-mode BatchNorm affines into their preceding convolutions (per-channel weight rescale, folded conv bias, BN module removed) removes the 20 aten.batch_norm kernels (43.84us, 6.0% of diagnostic CUDA time) and their eager dispatches from the timed forward while logits stay within atol=rtol=1e-4 with exact top-1, because the transform is algebraically exact up to FP32 rounding of the folded weights. Expected effect on latency_ms is a hypothesis to be A/B measured, not assumed: diagnostic CUDA durations are nested/inclusive, kernel-time savings do not by themselves imply wall-latency savings, and the gain exceeds ~6% only if the removed launches/dispatches sit on the critical path. Secondary, same-gate sub-hypothesis: a shape-preserving FP32 call-path or layout variant for the stage-3 conv sites (especially the 115.97us 256->512 stride-2 call and the 3x 512@7x7 calls, 204.13us) recovers part of their efficiency gap with no numerical-policy change. Acceptance requires paired median latency_ms improvement with unchanged logits/top-1 and peak-memory regression check; any tolerance failure or no measured latency gain rejects the candidate and triggers atomic fallback to the unmodified execution.
